subject: Critical Thinking
title: Decision Trees: Mapping Complex Choices
description: A quick, practical guide to Decision Trees: Mapping Complex Choices.

hook.text: Should you take the new job? It depends on salary, growth, location, risk – & how those interact.

buildup.text: A decision tree: a branching diagram where each node is a choice or chance event, & each branch has a probability &.

discovery.text: By multiplying probabilities along each path & comparing expected values, you can find the optimal choice.

twist.text: Trees force you to make assumptions explicit.

climax.text: Used in medicine (treatment decisions), business (investment choices), and AI (decision-making algorithms).

punchline.text: Draw the tree. Assign the numbers. The right choice often reveals itself.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of using a decision tree?
options: It makes assumptions explicit and allows mathematical comparison of options

details.summary: Decision trees visually map out choices, chance events, and outcomes in a branching structure. Each node forces you to consider probabilities and payoffs systematically, making complex decisions manageable.
details.whyItMatters: Decision trees transform overwhelming multi-step decisions into clear, analyzable structures that reveal which options have the highest expected value.
takeaways: Decision nodes represent choices; chance nodes represent uncertain events
Working backward from outcomes reveals optimal decisions
Trees make hidden assumptions and probabilities explicit

faq.question: How do you build a decision tree for a real-world problem?
faq.answer: Start with the initial decision, branch into possible choices, add chance nodes for uncertain outcomes with probabilities, assign values to final outcomes, then work backward multiplying probabilities by values to find the highest expected path.

faq.question: What are the limitations of decision trees in practice?
faq.answer: They require probability estimates that may be unreliable, they grow exponentially complex with many variables, and they assume rational value maximization which ignores emotional and ethical factors.
